knowledge_units.statement: Concept drift is a change over time in the predictive relationship between inputs and the target; therefore an observed increase in prediction error is a monitoring signal but is not by itself an identification of concept drift.
qualifiers: Error can reveal degraded performance, but the selected definition does not make any single error threshold a proof of relationship change.

knowledge_units.statement: Data-driven soft-sensor maintenance includes moving-window, recursive-adaptation, and ensemble approaches, but these are broad adaptation categories rather than a one-to-one taxonomy of fixed-base external correction versus base-model retraining.
qualifiers: Under this frozen Investigation, any method that uses new actual data to change base-model parameters belongs to model update/retraining. Only a post-prediction or otherwise external correction that leaves the base model parameters unchanged remains on the fixed-base branch.
The source review establishes the breadth of adaptation mechanisms; it does not establish that moving-window, recursive, or ensemble methods all preserve a frozen base model.

knowledge_units.statement: An industrial soft-sensor case combines a model-mismatch index with process-monitoring statistics such as T² and SPE to monitor degradation and guide model-update timing, then incorporates samples from new process conditions into the updated model.
qualifiers: This is a case-specific maintenance method and does not establish universal thresholds for mismatch, T², SPE, or retraining.

knowledge_units.statement: Production ML practice treats testing and monitoring as prerequisites for reliable model operation and maintenance rather than treating model updates as an unmanaged reaction to one performance metric.
qualifiers: The production-readiness evidence is cross-domain and does not itself specify process-control retraining thresholds.

knowledge_units.statement: Across the selected evidence, escalation from a frozen base model plus external correction toward base-model updating is best treated as a monitored model-maintenance decision: persistent post-correction mismatch should be interpreted together with evidence of changed process/predictive conditions rather than by raw prediction error alone. Broad adaptive-model categories are background context, not a separate fixed-base comparator when they change base-model parameters.
qualifiers: This is a methodological synthesis, not a universally published AND-rule or numerical trigger.

The frozen scope separately requires non-model causes (sensor/process/actuation/data pipeline) to be considered before attributing degradation to the base predictive relation; the selected evidence does not supply a complete diagnostic procedure for that branch.
The selected evidence does not directly compare a strictly frozen base model plus external post-prediction correction against retraining on the same industrial process.

relations.description: Performance degradation can motivate investigation, but model-mismatch/process-state evidence is needed to interpret whether the predictive relationship has actually changed.

The soft-sensor review and industrial case show that model maintenance can use multiple adaptation/update mechanisms and that update timing can be monitoring-driven; they do not define those mechanisms as fixed-base alternatives to retraining.

A defensible base-model update decision depends on monitoring sufficient to distinguish persistent mismatch from a transient metric excursion and to validate the subsequent maintenance action; the fixed-base versus parameter-updating classification remains governed by the frozen Investigation scope.

uncertainties.description: No selected evidence establishes process-independent numerical thresholds, persistence windows, or alarm levels at which base-model retraining becomes mandatory.

The frozen evidence does not provide a complete validated diagnostic procedure for separating model-relation change from sensor faults, actuation faults, data-pipeline defects, or other non-model causes of degraded prediction.
The selected evidence does not determine the minimum amount, coverage, or labeling quality of new-regime data required before a retrained candidate can be accepted.

The selected evidence does not provide a controlled head-to-head comparison, on the same target process, between continuing a strictly frozen base model with external post-prediction correction and performing a base-model parameter update/retraining.
